7408f96c9: leases._note_landed; 6 tests in tests/test_recover_merged_item.py, 3 fail on unfixed code

chunk_findings.detail: The model supplied to `CM.verdict` is computed from `state.sessions.values()` filtered only by `x.agent == rec.holder`, not restricted to the session for `it.id`. If `alice` held a lapsed lease on item A with model `gpt-4`, then later started a newer session on item B with model `gpt-5`, `_note_landed` selects `gpt-5`. `CM.verdict` compares reviewer independence against the passed model, so if A's reviewer also used `gpt-4`, the code can compute `may_complete=True` and advise `ddflow complete A` even though `ddflow complete A` using A's real session model would refuse for lack of independence. The function should filter by the current item's session identifier before taking the latest session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s own docstring says it exercises completion “against the lapsed lease,” but it never lapses the lease. The file’s only lapse mechanism is `_recs` passing `now=time.time() + later`; this test does not call `_recs`. It runs `pass_pipeline` and `LC.complete` immediately after `_merged`, which has just appended a fresh `session.started` for `worker`, so the lease is not in the lapsed state that generated the advice this test is supposed to validate. If `LC.complete` refuses to complete an expired lease, this test would still pass, meaning the suite would not catch that the newly advised command fails in the exact state `scan` reports.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:test_the_advised_path_works

chunk_findings.detail: The test checks that the new `ddflow complete T1` advice is present, but it never asserts the old `ddflow release T1` advice is absent. If the implementation merely appends the completion sentence to the existing “worktree is gone; nothing to salvage. `ddflow release`” message, this test passes even though the intent is “complete instead of release.” A regression that leaves both commands in the advice would go unnoticed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:test_a_merged_item_with_a_lapsed_lease_is_advised_to_complete

chunk_findings.detail: `model = max(mine, key=lambda x: x.started_at).model if mine else ""` chooses the most recent session for `rec.holder`, not the session belonging to `it.id`. If the same agent has more than one session in `state.sessions` (e.g. S1 for item 1 on GPT-4, S2 for item 2 on Claude, with S2 newer), `_note_landed` passes S2's model to `CM.verdict` for item 1. `CM.verdict` is specifically meant to reproduce what `ddflow complete {it.id}` would decide for that item, so the advice for item 1 can say complete will succeed or is refused based on the wrong model.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims “the diff, not the declared globs, decides,” but `_merged(repo, "T1", "docs/note.md")` declares the same docs glob as the diff, so diff-based and glob-based gate selection agree. It then explicitly records all named code gates as passed. A buggy implementation that ignored the diff and still owed the code gates would also make `LC.complete` succeed, so this test does not exercise the behavior its name promises.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:test_a_docs_only_item_is_not_owed_the_code_gates

chunk_findings.detail: The docstring says it records outcomes “against the lapsed lease,” but this test never advances time and never calls `_recs`; `_merged` returns immediately after `LC.merge`, so the original `worker` lease is still active. If `LC.complete` rejects completion while an active lease exists, the test would fail even though the intended post-lapse recovery path works, so it does not reproduce the state under test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:test_the_advised_path_works

chunk_findings.detail: The may_complete advice string hard-codes `(it also clears the lease)`, but `_note_landed` is also invoked from the `elif not lease and it.worktree and it.state != REVIEW` branch. For an item with no lease whose merge landed, whose worktree has nothing salvageable, and whose `CM.verdict` returns `may_complete=True`, recover will tell the user that `ddflow complete <id>` "also clears the lease" even though no lease exists for that item, which is false advice.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail: `_merged(repo, "T1", "docs/note.md", globs=[...])` creates an active lease held by `agent="worker"`. The test then records doc gates and immediately calls `LC.complete(repo, "T1", agent="rescuer", model="claude-opus-5")` without first calling `L.expire`. This is the same active-lease problem already confirmed and fixed in `test_the_advised_path_works` (line 77), but it was not applied here: a different agent attempts to complete an item whose lease is still active, so `LC.complete` refuses and line 105’s `assert out.exit == 0` fails. The test must lapse the lease before completing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:104 test_a_docs_only_item_is_not_owed_the_code_gates

chunk_findings.detail:
`mine = [x for x in state.sessions.values() if x.agent == rec.holder and x.model]`
selects the newest session *of any kind* for `rec.holder`, but the earlier triage records that
`ddflow complete` uses `_session_model`, the agent's latest **open** session. Given a holder with
an older open session on model A and a newer closed session on model B in `state.sessions`, this
code passes B to `CM.verdict`, while `complete` would pass A. Since `CM.verdict` uses the model for
reviewer-independence, recover can then say `ddflow complete {it.id}` will succeed or be refused
for the wrong reason, contradicting the promise that the advice mirrors `complete`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail:
In the `elif not lease and it.worktree and it.state != REVIEW:` call path there is no lease, but the
`v.may_complete` branch still appends `"(it also clears the lease)"`. An item with no lease, an
empty/unsalvageable worktree, a passed merge gate, and an on-base merge commit gets the advice that
complete "also clears the lease" when there is no lease for it to clear. The parenthetical is simply
false on this path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_docs_only_item_is_not_owed_the_code_gates` calls `LC.complete` while the `worker` lease created by `_merged` is still active. The round-1 findings established that `LC.complete` rejects completion in that state, and `test_the_advised_path_works` was fixed for exactly this reason by calling `L.expire` before `LC.complete`. This test has no `L.expire` (and no `_recs` time advance), so the correct implementation will still return a nonzero exit because the lease is not lapsed, and the final `assert out.exit == 0` fails before the test can exercise whether docs-only items are owed code gates.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:102

data.probe: pytest tests/test_recover_merged_item.py::test_a_docs_only_item_is_not_owed_the_code_gates passes: complete by another agent is not refused over a live lease
data.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:102

chunk_findings.detail: In the `else` refusal branch, the advice lists only `v.blockers[:3]` but then says “Record those outcomes …, then complete it.” If `CM.verdict` returns more than three blockers, the user is told to record only the first three and then expects `ddflow complete` to succeed, but the unlisted blockers still refuse completion. For example, an already-merged clean tree owing outcomes for code, tests, docs, and coverage gates would show only the first three; after recording those three, `ddflow complete` is still refused by the fourth.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed

chunk_findings.detail: The `not v.may_complete` advice says `ddflow complete {it.id}` and then “Record those outcomes (`ddflow gate status {it.id}`), then complete it” without `--model <author model>`. Concretely, if the holder has no open session with a model (`mine` is empty, so `CM.verdict` is called with `model=""`), `CM.verdict` can return `may_complete=False` with an unknown-author-model/reviewer-independence blocker. `ddflow gate status` records gate outcomes, not the author model, so a user who follows the advice to record outcomes and then runs the completion command as shown is still refused. The may-complete branch does include `--model`; the refused branch should include it too.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/leases.py:_note_landed refused branch

chunk_findings.detail: This test is the regression probe for confirmed finding 2, but it never reaches the branch that had the bug. It calls `_merged(repo, "T1", "src/T1/a.py", keep=True)` and then `L.release`, without `pass_pipeline(...)`. As `test_the_advice_names_what_complete_still_wants` in the same file shows, after `_merged` alone the item still owes non-merge required gates, so `_note_landed` follows its missing-gates branch. The erroneous `"(it also clears the lease)"` was appended only in the `v.may_complete` branch; therefore `assert "clears the lease" not in rec.advice` passes on the buggy code. The confirmed issue is not actually guarded by this probe.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:120 `test_a_kept_clean_tree_with_no_lease_is_advised_to_complete_without_a_lease_clause`

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not exercise the previously confirmed `blockers[:3]` truncation bug: it leaves a code item with no recorded outcomes and asserts only that `unit_tests` is mentioned. If the implementation still lists only the first three blockers and `unit_tests` is one of those three, this test still passes; it never produces more than three outstanding blockers and never checks the other required gates. That probe therefore does not answer the prior finding, and the exact defect can remain while this test is green.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_merged_item.py:test_the_advice_names_what_complete_still_wants
